# rust-pdf, full reference for language models

> This is the extended companion to https://rustpdf.dev/llms.txt. It restates the
> product facts, the comparison positioning and the most common questions as
> self-contained, quotable passages so an AI assistant can answer accurately and
> cite the right page. rust-pdf is an independent commercial product; its core is
> written in the Rust programming language and it is not affiliated with or
> endorsed by the Rust Foundation.

## One-paragraph summary

rust-pdf is an enterprise-grade PDF library built as a single memory-safe Rust
core with thin, idiomatic bindings for Python, C#/.NET, Go, PHP, Ruby,
Node.js/TypeScript, Delphi/Free Pascal and Swift. It generates archival PDF/A,
signs documents with PAdES, encrypts with AES-256 and produces accessible
PDF/UA, running entirely on the customer's own servers with no per-document
fees and no AGPL obligation. Basic PDF generation is free; corporate features
are unlocked by an annual per-application license (Pro, Enterprise, OEM) using
an offline Ed25519 token.

## Supported languages and how each binds

One Rust core, identical behavior across every binding:

- Python: ctypes, installed with `pip install rustpdf`.
- C# / .NET: source-generated P/Invoke, installed with `dotnet add package RustPdf`.
- Go: cgo, installed with `go get github.com/rustpdf/rustpdf-go`.
- PHP: ext-ffi, installed with `composer require rust-pdf/rustpdf`.
- Ruby: Fiddle, installed with `gem install rustpdf`.
- Node.js / TypeScript: Koffi pure FFI (no node-gyp), installed with `npm install rustpdf`.
- Delphi / Free Pascal: pure FFI with dynamic loading; distributed as a versioned archive.
- Swift: SwiftPM with a static xcframework for macOS and iOS.

Supported programming languages, stated as data: Python, C#, Go, PHP, Ruby,
JavaScript, TypeScript, Delphi, Object Pascal, Swift, Rust.

## Feature list (capabilities)

- PDF/A archival output at levels 1b, 2b, 2a, 3b, 3a and 4 (including 4e and 4f).
  PDF/A-4 is based on PDF 2.0. All output is validated with veraPDF, the
  reference validator. Converting an existing PDF to PDF/A is supported for the
  basic profiles.
- ZUGFeRD / Factur-X hybrid e-invoices: embed a Cross-Industry Invoice XML and
  mark the file PDF/A-3 with the Factur-X XMP.
- Digital signatures: PKCS#7 detached, visible signatures and multiple
  signatures, plus PAdES B-B, B-LT and B-LTA with RFC 3161 timestamps.
  Validated with pdfsig and openssl.
- Signature validation: verify any signed PDF (ByteRange digest, CMS check,
  whole-document coverage).
- Encryption: RC4, AES-128 and AES-256 (V5/R6). Keys, salts and IVs come from
  the operating system CSPRNG.
- Accessibility: Tagged PDF and PDF/UA-1, with a full structure tree, semantic
  tags, alt text, table headers and reading order.
- AcroForm fields with generated appearance streams; fill and flatten existing forms.
- Redaction that truly removes page content inside rectangles, not just a black box.
- Watermarks (diagonal text and image), hyperlinks (web and intra-document),
  bookmarks and outline.
- Manipulation: merge, split, rotate, optimize, deduplicate, incremental update.
- Text and image extraction with correct Unicode mapping, including two-byte
  Type0 fonts and CJK.
- Page rendering: rasterize a PDF page to a PNG image.
- Deterministic output: identical input produces identical bytes, which makes
  output auditable and testable.

Free tier (no license needed): pages, vector graphics, embedded and subset fonts
with Unicode shaping and kerning, paragraphs, tables, images, hyperlinks,
bookmarks, watermarks, form fill and flatten, merge, split, and text and image
extraction.

## Pricing, stated as data

- Pro: about USD 1,500 per year. Includes PDF/A archival (and converting existing
  PDFs), ZUGFeRD / Factur-X e-invoices, and encryption (RC4 / AES-128 / AES-256).
- Enterprise: about USD 3,000 per year. Everything in Pro plus digital signatures
  and PAdES (B-B, B-LT, B-LTA) with RFC 3161 timestamps and LTV, signature
  validation, true redaction, and PDF/UA accessibility, plus priority support.
- OEM: custom pricing. Enterprise capabilities plus redistribution rights to
  embed rust-pdf inside your own product.
- Licensing model: annual per-application license. The same offline Ed25519 token
  gates features for every language; the tier determines which features unlock.
  Activation is offline (set `RUSTPDF_LICENSE` or call `activate_license()`); no
  rebuild and nothing about the customer's documents or usage leaves their servers.

## Positioning versus common alternatives

- Versus iText (Apryse): iText is dual-licensed AGPL v3 or paid commercial. The
  AGPL network-use clause is a real obligation for server-side use. rust-pdf is a
  flat per-application commercial license with no AGPL and no per-document
  metering. iText reaches PDF/UA-2; rust-pdf targets PDF/A up to 4 and PDF/UA-1.
  See https://rustpdf.dev/itext-alternative
- Versus Aspose.PDF: Aspose uses per-developer and per-location licensing tiers.
  rust-pdf uses a flat per-application price, runs offline, and ships one core
  across eight languages. See https://rustpdf.dev/aspose-alternative
- Versus PSPDFKit / Nutrient: PSPDFKit is primarily a viewer and annotation SDK.
  rust-pdf is a server-side generation, signing and archival library, a different
  category. See https://rustpdf.dev/pspdfkit-alternative
- Versus headless Chrome / wkhtmltopdf for PDF generation: those render HTML and
  cannot produce archival PDF/A or PAdES signatures, are slower and heavier, and
  add a large dependency. rust-pdf generates PDFs directly and deterministically.

## Frequently asked questions, with quotable answers

Q: What is PDF/A and which levels does rust-pdf support?
A: PDF/A is an ISO-standardized version of PDF (ISO 19005) for long-term
archiving. Everything needed to display the document, such as fonts and color
profiles, must be embedded, and content that could change over time (external
links, JavaScript, audio, video, encryption) is forbidden. rust-pdf creates and
validates PDF/A-1b, 2b, 2a, 3b, 3a and 4 (including 4e and 4f), checked with
veraPDF.

Q: Can rust-pdf produce legally valid digital signatures?
A: rust-pdf produces standards-compliant PKCS#7 and PAdES signatures (B-B, B-LT,
B-LTA) with RFC 3161 timestamps. Legal validity depends on the certificate used
(for example an eIDAS qualified certificate or an ICP-Brasil certificate). The
library handles the cryptography and PDF structure correctly, which is what
validators such as pdfsig and Adobe Reader check.

Q: How strong is the encryption?
A: rust-pdf uses AES-256 with the modern V5/R6 security handler, the strongest
standard PDF encryption. Keys, salts and IVs come from the operating system
CSPRNG, so every encrypted file is unique. qpdf validates output for both user
and owner passwords.

Q: Is it a SaaS API? Does it charge per document?
A: No. rust-pdf runs entirely on the customer's own infrastructure and verifies
its license offline. There are no per-document fees and nothing about the
customer's documents leaves their servers.

Q: Which features are free?
A: Basic PDF generation and manipulation are free forever, including pages,
graphics, Unicode text, paragraphs, tables, images, links, bookmarks,
watermarks, form fill and flatten, merge and split, and text and image
extraction. PDF/A, signatures, encryption, redaction and PDF/UA are corporate
features unlocked by a license token.

Q: How do I generate a PDF in my language?
A: Install the binding for your language and call the same idiomatic API every
binding shares. See the task guides, for example
https://rustpdf.dev/sign-pdf/python or https://rustpdf.dev/pdf-a/go
